Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test reads entries from a 7z archive that includes entries of size 0. It asserts that calling SevenZFile.read() on those zero-length entries returns -1, indicating EOF, while other entries return data bytes (not -1). The issue is described in the bug report: calling read() on empty entries throws IllegalStateException instead of behaving properly.

Inspecting the SevenZFile.read() method shows it delegates to an InputStream returned by getCurrentStream(). The getCurrentStream() throws an IllegalStateException if deferredBlockStreams is empty. The bug report indicates this happens for zero-length entries due to changes in buildDecodingStream().

Looking at buildDecodingStream(), it checks the folder index of the current entry. If folderIndex < 0 (which can happen for empty entries or entries without data), it clears deferredBlockStreams and returns without adding any stream. Consequently, deferredBlockStreams stays empty for such entries.

Later, when read() is called on that entry, getCurrentStream() throws IllegalStateException because deferredBlockStreams is empty, as there's no stream corresponding to the empty entry.

The test fails here because the code assumes even empty entries have a stream that returns EOF (-1) on read, but in reality no stream is constructed, causing an exception.

Thus, the root cause is that for empty entries, buildDecodingStream() clears deferredBlockStreams and does not add a stream, which means calling read() on these entries results in an IllegalStateException instead of EOF.

This diagnosis matches the symptoms in the report and test:
- Empty entries cause folderIndex < 0, deferredBlockStreams cleared.
- No stream added for the empty entry.
- read() fails with IllegalStateException due to empty deferredBlockStreams.
- The test expects read() to safely return -1 on zero-sized entries but this is broken.

Recent bug reports about similar archive issues with entry sizes or streams also support that handling of size 0 or special cases in decoding streams might have been affected by changes.

Hence, the root cause is improper handling of empty entries in SevenZFile.buildDecodingStream(), where no InputStream is created or added to deferredBlockStreams, causing read() calls to fail with IllegalStateException.

This indicates that buildDecodingStream() should be updated to provide a consistent empty InputStream for zero-sized entries instead of clearing deferredBlockStreams with no stream, to prevent the exception and fix reading empty entries as the test expects.
